dossier.public_summary: TESS shows three consistent 2-hour, flat-bottomed dips every 11 days on a quiet nearby M dwarf giving a ~2.9 Earth-radius signal that fits the star's duration. No odd-even difference, no secondary eclipse and no nearby star within a pixel can mimic it. The period lies near 4.5 times the star's spin, but the total variability is only 10% of the transit depth and the shape remains transit-like, consistent with a small planet.

reasons.why: Planet-sized (below 10 Rearth), undiluted depth 5450 ppm and rp/rstar 0.07382; duration ratio 0.9763 fits central duration 2.048 h with b 0.1839

Strongly flat-bottomed (negative v_sigma favours box), with best_ingress_fraction 0.05 and t14_h 2.2; combined with steady transit_depths (p_consistent 0.6682, chi2 0.806, 3 transits consistent) this is a transit, not noise from a few events
No plausible NEB within one TESS pixel and quiet phase curve (amplitude_ppm 583.9, ratio_to_depth 0.1077, chi2 13.24 dof 9) with no secondary < 5 sigma
